paper.title_en: Spontaneous Chiral Superradiance of a Spin-1 Condensate in a Ring Cavity
paper.abstract_en: We investigate superradiant phase transitions in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to a ring cavity, where two symmetry-related Raman processes couple the atomic spin states to counterpropagating cavity modes. Above the superradiant threshold, we find that the symmetry between the two Raman channels is spontaneously broken, giving rise to a chiral superradiant (CSR) phase. Despite the exchange symmetry of the Hamiltonian, the CSR state spontaneously selects one of the two propagation directions, with one cavity mode becoming macroscopically occupied while its counterpropagating partner remains dark. Spin-dependent collisions further reshape the superradiant phase diagram by selectively shifting the boundaries between the chiral and symmetric superradiant phases, a feature intrinsic to the multicomponent spin-$1$ manifold. For sufficiently negative spin-dependent interactions, the interaction-induced modification of the atomic level structure gives rise to a reversed plane-wave phase characterized by an inverted internal-state occupation. These results identify spontaneous selection between symmetry-related superradiant channels as a mechanism for generating chirality in many-body cavity QED and demonstrate how spin-dependent collisions control the resulting superradiant phase structure.
